research_mode: official ONS sexual-offences survey and police-recorded methodology only; sample, age-range, legislation, reporting and demand gates; no parcel, exact-location, candidate or business result claimed

sources.name: Sexual-offence source families
verified_claims: The sexual-offences overview uses the Crime Survey for England and Wales and police-recorded crime.
limitations: Survey and police measures have different coverage and must remain separately labelled.

sources.name: Preferred victimisation measure
verified_claims: ONS identifies the CSEW as the best measure of sexual victimisation prevalence.
limitations: The survey does not measure exact police workload or parcel-specific events.

sources.name: Last-year sexual-assault prevalence
verified_claims: An estimated 1.9% of people aged 16 years and over, around 900,000 people, experienced sexual assault including attempts in the year ending March 2025.
limitations: A survey estimate is not an exact count of incidents or addresses.

sources.name: Female and male prevalence
verified_claims: Estimated last-year prevalence was 3.0% among females and 0.7% among males.
limitations: Group rates must not be converted into individual predictions.

sources.name: Since-age-16 sexual-assault prevalence
verified_claims: Approximately 15.9% of people aged 16 years and over, around 7.7 million people, had experienced sexual assault since age 16.
limitations: Lifetime prevalence and last-year prevalence are different measures.

sources.name: Since-age-16 rape prevalence
verified_claims: An estimated 4.0% of people aged 16 years and over had experienced rape including attempts since age 16.
limitations: Survey categories include attempts and should not be equated with police offence counts.

sources.name: Partner or ex-partner relationship
verified_claims: Among victims of rape or assault by penetration since age 16, 54.7% reported a partner or ex-partner as the perpetrator of the most recent incident.
limitations: Survey relationship proportions do not identify an individual offender or location.

sources.name: Police-reporting proportion
verified_claims: Around 14.7% of victims of rape or assault by penetration since age 16 reported the most recent assault to police.
limitations: Police records capture only a fraction of survey-estimated victimisation.

sources.name: Half-sample quality warning
verified_claims: Year ending March 2025 sexual-assault estimates are based on a half sample.
limitations: Reduced sample size increases uncertainty and requires caution.

sources.name: Comparable age-range series
verified_claims: ONS uses ages 16 to 59 for long-term comparison after removal of the survey upper age limit in October 2021.
limitations: All-adult and 16-to-59 estimates must not be treated as identical populations.

sources.name: Pandemic survey gap
verified_claims: No year ending March 2021 CSEW sexual-assault data are available because face-to-face surveying was suspended during the pandemic.
limitations: The missing year must not be interpolated as observed data.

sources.name: Year ending March 2022 quality status
verified_claims: Year ending March 2022 estimates are not designated accredited official statistics because of reduced collection and lower response rates.
limitations: The 2022 point requires explicit quality qualification in trends.

sources.name: Year ending March 2023 reduced period
verified_claims: Year ending March 2023 estimates use eight months of data because a survey error caused missing data.
limitations: The shortened period affects precision and comparability.

sources.name: Year ending March 2024 half sample
verified_claims: Year ending March 2024 and March 2025 estimates are based on half samples.
limitations: Year comparisons must account for reduced sample quality.

sources.name: Police-recorded trend limitation
verified_claims: Police-recorded sexual offences do not provide a reliable trend measure because reporting, recording and offence definitions have changed.
limitations: Recorded increases must not automatically be interpreted as prevalence increases.

sources.name: Police-recorded sexual-offence total
verified_claims: Police recorded 209,079 sexual offences in the year ending March 2025, an 11% increase from the previous year.
limitations: The total is police demand and recorded offences, not survey prevalence.

sources.name: Online Safety Act offence effect
verified_claims: Two offences introduced by the Online Safety Act 2023 accounted for over half of the annual increase in recorded sexual offences.
limitations: The increase partly reflects newly captured offences rather than a like-for-like rise.

sources.name: Police sexual-offence scope
verified_claims: Police-recorded sexual offences include rape, sexual assault, sexual activity with minors, child sexual exploitation and other offences.
limitations: The police category is broader than the CSEW sexual-assault measure.

sources.name: Sexual-offence under-reporting
verified_claims: Under-reporting to police is particularly acute for sexual offences, so many more offences occur than are recorded by police.
limitations: An absence of police records must not be interpreted as absence of victimisation.

sources.name: Survey and police-demand distinction
verified_claims: The CSEW provides the best prevalence trend estimate but cannot be used to infer demand on police services.
limitations: Prevalence and operational-demand metrics must remain separate.
